newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares slip on selective stocks falls.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares slip on selective stocks falls.

text.p: Shanghai B shares slipped on falls in selective stocks on Wednesday with a wait-to-see mood still dominating the market, brokers said.
The index dropped 0.410 points or 0.84 percent to 48.487 points on volume of 7.8 million shares worth $2.2 million. Of 41 B shares, 34 traded with nine down, 12 flat and 13 up.
Brokers said falls in Shanghai Shangling and Eastern Commminications pulled the index down, but it meant little with most investors remaining on the sidelines on a lack of market-moving news.
Shanghai Shangling Electric Appliance was the biggest loser on last minutes speculative selling, plunging $0.058 or 15.18 percent to $0.324 on volume of just 12,000 shares.
Eastern Communications became the second-worst performer after a speculative surge yesterday, tumbling $0.084 or 10.71 percent to $0.700 on volume of 523,000 shares.
"Trading was very sluggish, so any speculative selling or buying can push the market up or down easily, which made the market less attractive to foreign investors," one broker said.
"Today's falls worsen the technical charts and the index will test the 48 points support level in the coming days," a second broker said.
Shanghai Automation Instrumentation traded the most on institutional cross-trading, ending unchanged at $0.130 on volume of 542,000 shares.
Shanghai A shares continued their correction after sharp gains in the past few days, but market sentiment was bullish with trading active, brokers said.
The A index fell 3.480 points or 0.35 percent to 981.862 points on volume of 797.2 million shares worth 6.6 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index edged up 0.025 points to 2540.110 points.
Jinbei Automotive was the biggest loser, falling 0.27 yuan or 6.47 percent to 3.90 yuan on volume of 32.4 million shares.
